title: Control Panel, clock, screen blanker (kernel/ctrl.inc, clock.inc, clockw.inc, blank.inc; SPEC.md 31, 37, 64, 76, 79)
summary: The area is structurally sound and mostly costs no resident memory. The Control Panel is the on-demand CTRL.DRV (15,405 bytes on kern_big today) behind small resident gates, the RTC ladder runs in the boot overlay, its write half ships in the module, and the blanker gates the video signal with the animated saver falling back to it on every failure. The main real defect is that the clock gains about 31 s/day: clk_tick divides by 18.2 where the rate is 18.2065, and the fix (x625/11379) costs 0 bytes. Two narrower defects: a hostile SYSTEM.CFG 'CH' byte above 1 lets the Date/Time page step a kernel .bss byte 254 past clk_sec (a 5-byte overlay fix), and the time the user sets never reaches 40:6C, so the kernel's DOS shows a different time and date from the menu bar on an XT (WIN16 already reads OSAPI_CLK_GET and agrees). The biggest weakness is prose drift: SPEC.md 31/37/64/76/79 and several file headers still describe retired designs (140px panel with no KD_INIT and no .bss, a 32-byte file, caption-reported save errors, a month table and a month mask, an RTC drained by ui_task, unpersisted display settings, kern_small carrying saver bytes); the verified fixes are in doc_fixes. Two rethinks are worth the owner's time: R1, derive time of day from the BIOS count at 40:6C as DOS does (one clock, no drift, no 59-minute saver ceiling, roughly neutral bytes, no ABI), and R2, declarative page tables driven by one engine (Mac DITL / Windows DLGTEMPLATE / GEOS generic UI), an unprototyped 1.5-3 KB off CTRL.DRV with 0 resident cost. KHP_RELIT on kern_big (sysmisc-9) is already measured and queued in docs/plans/LAST-DROP-PERF.md.

strengths.title: RTC ladder ordered so no rung writes a chip a later rung might identify differently
strengths.why: Read-only probes run first, the RP5C01 is claimed only on agreement with the BIOS, and the MM58167 probe has a 4-bit veto before its single scratch write. It finds XT clock cards that DOS needed ASTCLOCK-style drivers for, and the probe discipline is worth copying.

strengths.title: Hybrid UIP + seconds guard on the AT read; the write half obeys the machine's own conventions
strengths.why: This is Linux's converged read guard, with a DM-bit fallback. The write never forces DM or 24/12, preserves the RP5C01 alarm bit, and invents no century byte.

strengths.title: Snapshot discipline for the clock
strengths.why: Each carrying write is one cli section per second, and readers format from one snapshot. An hour of catch-up never holds interrupts off for long.

strengths.title: Resident gates in front of the module
strengths.why: Once-a-second and every-close questions are answered from resident bytes, so CTRL.DRV is never read off a floppy to learn that nothing is showing.

strengths.title: One page ladder serves as hit test and action (cp_probe 0/1/2), with id-0 selecting sites
strengths.why: There is no second copy of any page's geometry, and safe prefix actions keep the press per SPEC.md 13.6.

strengths.title: Record vs ordinal separation in the item list
strengths.why: A hidden row can sit anywhere, and [cp_sel] names something durable while ordinals are derived.

strengths.title: Deferred single SYSTEM.CFG write, with retry on failure
strengths.why: The effect is immediate and the record waits for the close. That fits a machine where one write is about 2 s of frozen UI.

strengths.title: Signal-gated blank, the always-available fallback
strengths.why: Wake is instant and exact, no drawing path carries a test, and background tasks keep drawing. Windows savers paint and pay a full repaint on wake.

strengths.title: Wake input consumed; the ring drained, not reset
strengths.why: Treated as a safety rule. EVT_WAKE records are owed rather than lost.

strengths.title: SAVER.DRV reuses the driver loader via a row-shaped record; the overlay is asked, never volunteers
strengths.why: There is no second loader, and freeing code that still has to return is impossible by construction.

strengths.title: WF_QUIET chooses blank-instead-of-saver, never none
strengths.why: A leaked flag leaves the monitor dark, not lit. This is the correct inversion of Windows' SC_SCREENSAVE veto.

strengths.title: Mirrored constants and offsets are gated
strengths.why: t_mirror and the SS_IDLE_AT assert turn a no-linker interface into a build failure.

findings.title: System clock gains ~31 s/day: clk_tick divides by 18.2 Hz instead of 18.2065
findings.detail: clk_tick computes seconds as delta*10/182, but [ticks] runs at 1193182/65536 = 18.20648 Hz (the BIOS day is 1,573,040 ticks). Each counted second is 0.99964 s of wall time: +0.0356%, about +30.8 s/day or 3.6 min/week. Nothing corrects it (no RTC re-read after boot; no RTC at all on a 5150). The Timer app's stopwatch has the same constant. kerndos does not accumulate the error because it re-derives the time of day from 40:6C on every call (its 32,772 half-ticks an hour costs at most about a second within the hour).
evidence: kernel/clock.inc:1663-1667 'what makes 18.2 Hz add up to real seconds'
SPEC.md 64.1 '[ticks], the BIOS counter at 18.2065 Hz'
findings.recommendation: Use mov dx,625 / mov cx,11379 (11379/625 = 18.20640, error 4.5e-6, about 0.4 s/day). Same encoding sizes. Overflow: 65535*625+11378 < 2^32 and the quotient is at most 3600; hibernation's 32768-tick passes stay in range. Update clk_acc's comment (a 1/625-tick remainder) and SPEC.md 37 Advancing. Apply the same fix to the Timer package.
findings.prior_art: DOS derives time of day from the BIOS tick count and so inherits the BIOS's exact day.
findings.verify_note: Re-read clk_tick (clock.inc:1678-1693): mul 10 / div 182 against [ticks], which every IRQ0 path bumps at the BIOS rate (sched.inc:2262; fsx.inc:1397-1409 keeps [ticks] and 40:6C exact under FSXF_RATE). Arithmetic checked: +30.8 s/day; 625/11379 gives 0.39 s/day, both immediates are imm16 so 0 bytes, worst case 65535*625+11378 = 40,970,753 fits DX:AX with quotient 3600. Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST, KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE or FIELD-NOTES. Predicted, not measured on a 5150.

findings.title: Hostile SYSTEM.CFG 'CH' byte > 1 lets the Date/Time page step a .bss byte 254 past clk_sec
findings.detail: The unpack copies mapped bytes raw. Every reader of clk_h12 outside the page tests for zero, but the page uses it as a COUNT. cp_time_rows draws fields 0..5+h12, so 2 draws an 8th field with x/w/y read from bytes past cp_tflds' seven records. cp_time_pick can hit-test that field, so cp_tsel becomes 7. clk_fld_adj(7) then computes bl=5-7=0FEh, reads its range from [cs:0x1FC+clk_frng], and steps [clk_sec+254]: kernel .bss corruption from a floppy plus a click. xor 1 does not repair it (2 becomes 3). kern_big only: kern_small reads no SYSTEM.CFG.
evidence: kernel/clock.inc:2343-2344 osapi_clk_get_x already masks bit 0 for this reason
findings.recommendation: Normalise at the unpack: and byte [clk_h12],1 after the map loop (5 bytes). Optionally give CFG_MAP a per-key mask for the boolean keys.
findings.verify_note: Traced clk_fld_adj with AL=7: cmp al,6 fails, inc bx gives BL=5, sub gives 0FEh, shl/shr index clk_frng+0x1FC and [clk_sec+0FEh] - exactly as described; _deser/_unpack do no range check. Correction: _unpack is in the CFG_BOOT macro, instantiated for the overlay only (driver.inc:4910, 5403; CTRL.DRV gets CFG_SHARED/CFG_SAVE, 6257-6258), so the fix is one 5-byte store in .ovl, not two.

findings.title: The user's clock setting never reaches 40:6C, so the kernel's DOS disagrees with the menu bar
findings.detail: clock.inc promises 'one date + time of day for the whole system'. kerndos takes the time of day from 0040:006C and the date from int 1Ah AH=04h (CLK_DEF fallback). The kernel never writes 40:6C, and clk_rtc_write is its only outward push. On a 5150 with no clock card, a time set in the Control Panel is invisible to DOS: TIME reads time since power-on and DATE reads 4 July 2026. On an AT, DOS's time stays at the POST value plus uptime until the next boot. (WIN16 is not affected: its int 21h 2Ah/2Ch answer off OSAPI_CLK_GET, SPEC.md 124.17.3.)
evidence: kernel/clock.inc:4-5 'one date + time of day for the whole system'
apps/dos/dos.asm:14098-14135 dos_time_now from the tick count
kernel/ctrl.inc:5485-5496 cp_flush_close_x writes only the RTC
grep: no write to 0x046C in kernel/ outside mega.inc's PM tick maintenance
findings.recommendation: In cp_flush_close_x, when [clk_dirty], set the BIOS count with int 1Ah AH=01h (every PC BIOS, the 5150's included) from h:m:s x 18.2065, regardless of [clk_rtc], and clear 40:70. For the date, kerndos should ask OSAPI_CLK_GET (DOS area), as WIN16 already does. R1 (sysmisc-14) fixes this by construction.
findings.bytes_est: +~40-60 CTRL.DRV (a 32-bit h*65543 + m*1092 + s*18.2 sum and the int 1Ah call), 0 resident
findings.prior_art: DOS: one clock, the BIOS count, for every consumer.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed: dos_time_now/dos_ticks read 40:6C and dos_date_init asks int 1Ah AH=04h; cp_flush_close_x only calls clk_rtc_write; no kernel write to 46Ch. Correction: the byte estimate (~35) is low for a 32-bit tick count built from three fields; WIN16 already takes OSAPI_CLK_GET, which is the precedent for the kerndos date half.

findings.title: MM58167 New-Year shadow refreshed only on a Set or a roll, not on each boot
findings.detail: The last-month shadow at 09h is written only by clk_ns_write or when clk_ns_roll fires. Example: set in March, so the shadow is 3. Booted in December: no roll, correct. Off until the next April: 4 is not below 3, so no roll and the year reads one low. Refreshing the shadow at the December boot (to 12) would have caught it. The failure window should be 'off 12+ months', not 'any later month after the last Set'.
findings.recommendation: In clk_ns_read, call clk_ns_stamp whenever the shadow (decoded) differs from [clk_tb_mo], not only on a roll. The chip is already identified when this runs.
findings.verify_note: clk_ns_read stamps only when [clk_nsrol]; clk_ns_roll rolls only when the shadow is above the current month. The March-set, April-next-year case misses as described. SPEC.md 37.90 promises 'a machine switched off over New Year come back right', which holds only within a year of the last Set.

findings.title: RP5C01 claimed or refused depending on the time of day when the chip runs 12-hour
findings.detail: The probe joins the 10-hour digit with its PM bit, so afternoon hours read 20..39 and the 12 o'clock hours 12 and 32, never equal to the BIOS's 0 or 12..23. The same machine is rung 3 in the morning and falls to the BIOS rung in the afternoon, and the Date/Time caption and the write path change with it.
evidence: kernel/clock.inc:1305-1315 comment admits PM never matches
findings.recommendation: When the raw hour is above 23, also compare the 12-hour decode ((tens&1)*10+units, 12->0, +12 if PM bit). No page switch and no write, so the read-only promise holds.
findings.verify_note: clk_rp_probe compares the joined hour to [clk_rf_h] with no 12-hour decode; the comment calls the refusal deliberate but does not note that morning readings match, so the verdict depends on the hour. Only a chip left in 12-hour mode is affected.

findings.title: Screen Saver settings window outlives the Control Panel; its Customize sibling does not
findings.detail: THMPAL.DRV's window is closed and released in drv_cp_closed_x at every panel close. SAVER.DRV's window is unowned and reaped only through ss_post_x. With the panel closed, its Ok sets [cp_wdirty] with nobody to spend it; the save waits for the next panel close or reboot and a power-off loses it. This contradicts SPEC.md 79.7's 'the Control Panel's own close is what writes SYSTEM.CFG', and two buttons on one page behave differently.
evidence: kernel/driver.inc:3083-3097 THMPAL reaped at panel close
findings.recommendation: Close the saver window from the panel's teardown with a new SSV_* verb (mirrored, t_mirror-gated; DRVC_OVL is kernel-private, so no package ABI). Or let ss_post_x flush when cp_live finds no panel open.
findings.verify_note: grep finds no SSV_* or ss_reap_x call on the panel-close path; drv_cp_closed_x reaps only thmv_row. ss_post_x sets [cp_wdirty] unconditionally.

findings.title: Unloading VESA.DRV redraws the Drivers pane at a stale origin after vid_switch
findings.detail: cp_vid_click calls it load-bearing that nothing is redrawn after a switch, because DI/BP may describe a rectangle that no longer exists. The Drivers page's VID_EXT unload arm (default kern_big) switches to VGA and then runs cp_list, cp_drv_box1 and cp_drv_line1 at the pre-switch origin before cp_repost's full repaint. The result is a transient double-draw at old-mode coordinates.
evidence: kernel/ctrl.inc:7161-7179 cp_list / cp_drv_box1 / cp_drv_line1 at stale DI/BP
kernel/kernel.asm:858-861 VID_EXT on by default on kern_big
findings.recommendation: After the vesa_row switch, record the unload and want/answer and cp_wdset, then jmp .done past the redraw.
findings.verify_note: The .novx path falls into drv_unload_x, .off, .save and then cp_list/cp_drv_box1/cp_drv_line1 with the DI/BP computed before CPXF vid_switch. Transient only - cp_repost's repaint follows.

findings.title: 'cp_ctl before any side effect' and 'painter id = click id' are held by prose
findings.detail: Static page clicks run up to three times per gesture (act / identify / press). They are correct only if every action site reaches cp_ctl/cp_ctli before writing anything, and if each painter's BH id equals the click's id. All 25 sites read correctly today, but two once shipped without the call and no gate checks either property.
evidence: kernel/ctrl.inc:2058-2061 two sites shipped with no cp_ctl
findings.recommendation: R2 removes both invariants. Short of it, add an os88ovlchk-style flow check: the first DS store in each CPITEM click proc is dominated by a cp_ctl* call.
findings.verify_note: Low-severity record item; not re-walked across all 25 sites.

findings.title: kern_big's saver wake and fsx exit relight is a full wm_paint_all; the damage-pass version is kern_mega-only
findings.detail: blk_relit takes the damage pass only under KHP_RELIT, which only kern_mega defines. The XT build pays SPEC.md 11.91.7's 7-8x overdraw on every saver wake and every fullscreen exit. This is already priced: docs/plans/LAST-DROP-PERF.md row 2 measured KHP_RELIT at +32 bytes for CGA 781 -> 629 ms, Hercules 984 -> 727 and VGA 1,203 -> 706 per relight, and left it out of that round only to keep the round near 100 bytes.
findings.recommendation: Take LAST-DROP-PERF.md's row 2 as it stands: +32 resident bytes on kern_big for 150-500 ms per relight. Decide on bytes, not rungs.
findings.verify_note: The code is as described, but the finding's 'not measured here' and '~22 bytes' are superseded: LAST-DROP-PERF.md:589 already records +32 bytes and the per-adapter relight times. The item is queued there; this is a reminder, not a new finding.

findings.title: Dead boot-overlay stores and comments resting on a false '.bss is not zeroed'
findings.detail: clk_probe zeroes [clk_tier], [clk_cent] and [clk_ref] 'because .bss is not zeroed'. Kernel .bss arrives zeroed (SPEC.md 2.5, kernel.asm:5894-5896), clk_probe runs once (from clk_init), and clk_ref lives in clk_str, which is unwritten before the probe. The same false premise is repeated in clockw.inc and ctrl.inc (three places), contradicting blank.inc:121-123 which has it right.
findings.recommendation: Drop the three stores (or keep them and fix the comment), and correct the comments so they distinguish kernel .bss (zeroed) from a module image's data. The comment half is in doc_fixes.
findings.verify_note: clk_tier/clk_cent are outside clk_init's zeroed run (clock.inc:2233-2235) but .bss boots zero; the only clk_probe call is clock.inc:250. ctrl.inc's flagged bytes are resident .text (section .text at :277 and :5572), so the '-f bin zeroes nothing' reason is wrong for them too.

findings.title: Saver idle period capped at 59 minutes by the 16-bit tick compare
findings.detail: [ss_idle] is a word of ticks against the 16-bit [ticks], hence SS_MAXMIN 59, mirrored into the overlay's field. Windows 3.1 offered 1-99. Nothing needs more today.
findings.recommendation: Leave it unless R1 lands, which provides a 32-bit count for free.
findings.verify_note: SS_MAXMIN equ 59 and the clamp in ss_mins2idle (blank.inc:609-631) as described.

findings.title: W_FLAGS 'visible' bit is the literal 2 at about thirty sites
findings.detail: wm.inc names every other W_FLAGS bit but not bit 1, so 'visible' tests are ungreppable.
findings.recommendation: Add WF_VIS equ 2 and use it.
findings.verify_note: Real, but the count is about thirty (grep for `W_FLAGS], 2` returns 31 lines in kernel/, wm.inc itself carrying most), not eleven. No WF_VIS exists.

findings.title: A newly selected list row's name blinks into its bar
findings.detail: cp_listrow fills the 12px bar and then letters the name over it, so on the row gaining the selection the name vanishes into black for the fill-to-font_run gap. That is PERFORMANCE.md rule 2 at row scale. The cheap fixes cost more calls than they save.
findings.recommendation: Record only. A font_run variant with a vertical pad would be the right fix if one is ever wanted elsewhere.
findings.verify_note: cp_listrow: .bar's cp_fill then .name's cw_font_run on the selected row; the skip applies only to an unselected row under cp_lfull.

findings.title: R1: one clock - derive the time of day from 0040:006C
findings.detail: The kernel integrates its own clock (clk_last, clk_acc, a per-second carry, and a hibernation catch-up walking clk_last back 32768 ticks a pass). DOS, kerndos and the BIOS use 40:6C, which sch_isr keeps by chaining the ROM every tick and mega.inc maintains in PM. Keep only the date plus the last 40:6C seen, derive h:m:s on format (once a minute or second), detect midnight as count < last, and write the count via int 1Ah AH=01h. This removes sysmisc-1, sysmisc-3 and sysmisc-11, the accumulator, and hiber.inc's catch-up loop. Caveats for the prototype: a nested tick skips the ROM chain (sch_chskip, SPEC.md 8.5.1), so 40:6C can trail [ticks] by the skips; a DOS program's AH=01h/2Dh would then set the desktop's clock too; and the BIOS's midnight flag at 40:70 has two readers to coordinate.
evidence: kernel/sched.inc:2226-2232 and fsx.inc:1439-1442 the nested-tick skip
apps/dos/dos.asm:14098-14135 the three-divide breakdown already exists
findings.recommendation: Prototype: a ~45-byte breakdown shared by clk_fmt and osapi_clk_get_x replaces ~55 bytes of accumulator and sec/min/hour carry. OSAPI_CLK_GET's outputs are unchanged; KDL_CLK is internal. Count sch_chskip on the target before relying on the ROM's count.
findings.bytes_est: -10 to +10 resident (ESTIMATED); the AH=01h writer in CTRL.DRV
findings.prior_art: DOS (time = BIOS count); Mac (one 32-bit seconds counter, Secs2Date on demand); OS/2 1.x (time in the global info segment, read without a call).
findings.verify_note: Sound as a proposal; the ROM is chained every tick on both ISRs and hiber.inc relies on that. Added the nested-tick skip caveat (sched.inc .tskip / fsx.inc .tskip skip the ROM chain but still bump [ticks]).

findings.title: R2: declarative Control Panel pages driven by one engine
findings.detail: Static pages are about 150 hand-placed equates, a paint and a click ladder each, per-page control painters, and three prose-held invariants (probe-before-act, painter id = click id, one greying predicate). Every page uses the same five species (radio group, check, button, drop-down, labelled value). A {species, rect, id, getter, setter, predicate} table per page plus one engine of roughly 500-700 bytes would paint, hit-test, press/drag/release and grey from one description. Bespoke parts (Display slot compaction, Covox ports, the memory column) keep a callback hook. CTRL.DRV is 15,405 bytes on kern_big today (build/ctrl.drv); SPEC.md 2.8's 11,119 is a figure from an earlier size pass.
findings.recommendation: Do the static pages now: they are module-internal, with no ABI. Consider the driver-page ABI (DSV_CPPAINT/DSV_CPCLICK -> tables) for the flag-day list only once the engine has proven itself.
findings.prior_art: Mac DITL plus the Dialog Manager; Windows DLGTEMPLATE plus CheckRadioButton; PC/GEOS declarative UI compiled to generic objects (the closest 8088 peer).
findings.verify_note: The idea stands; the size evidence was stale. build/ctrl.drv is 15,405 bytes now, so the saving is a smaller share than the finding implied, and the estimate has no prototype behind it.

findings.title: A setting change reaches packages only as a world repaint
findings.detail: cp_repost sets [cp_dirty], and ui_task does wm_paint_all. A package caching derived state (OSAPI_CLK_GET's 12-hour bit, theme pens, the dock edge) has no notice beyond the repaint. Windows broadcast WM_WININICHANGE/WM_SYSCOLORCHANGE.
findings.recommendation: Record. If a package ever caches a setting, add an additive EVT_SETTING record posted by cp_repost.
findings.verify_note: cp_repost is a word store plus inc [ui_post] and nothing else (ctrl.inc:2866-2869).

findings.title: Core settings in battery-backed CMOS (Mac PRAM model) - considered, not recommended
findings.detail: The Mac kept core settings in 20 bytes of PRAM, written immediately. AT CMOS has bytes outside the checksum (often 34h-3Fh), but they are vendor-specific and the XT target has no CMOS.
findings.recommendation: Do not adopt. Recorded so it is not re-derived.
findings.verify_note: Prior-art record; nothing to verify in code.

doc_fixes.old_text:
**Month LENGTHS are not a table.** `clk_mlen` carries the eleven non-February
answers as one 16-bit mask — bit *m* set means month *m* has 31 days, *m* =
1..12, so bit 0 is unused and bit 2 is clear because February is the branch
under it. That is three bytes less than the `db 31,28,31,…` it replaced and
one review problem more, so `tests/unit/t_mlen.py` (fast tier) reads the
immediate back out of `build/kernel.bin` and asserts all twelve lengths —
doc_fixes.new_text:
**Month LENGTHS are not a table.** `clk_mlen` derives the eleven non-February
answers from the month's parity about August (kernel size pass 17): a month
has 31 days when it is odd below August and even from August on, so `cmp al,
8 / adc al, 0 / and al, 1 / xor al, 31`. February is the branch in front of
it. That replaced a 16-bit mask, which replaced the `db 31,28,31,…`, and each
step was one review problem more, so `tests/unit/t_mlen.py` (fast tier) reads
the routine back out of `build/kernel.bin` and asserts all twelve lengths —
doc_fixes.why: clock.inc:1816-1820 is the parity form; tests/unit/t_mlen.py:9-14 documents both rewrites.

as `CFG_ANIM` is (§76.11). A floppy moves between machines and between
kernels, and a setting silently dropped by the build that cannot use it comes
back as a *different* setting on the build that can.
doc_fixes.new_text:
**The three bytes are `kern_big`'s** (kernel size pass 13): `kern_small` reads
and writes no `SYSTEM.CFG` (§51.5) and has no saver page, so nothing there
names them and its `[ss_idle]` stays at `BLK_IDLE`. They used to be carried in
every build, on the argument that a setting silently dropped by the build
that cannot use it comes back as a *different* setting on the build that can;
a build that reads no file drops nothing.
doc_fixes.why: ss_pub..ss_post are inside %ifdef KERN_BIG; kern_small keeps one parity byte (blank.inc:150-165).

A `'TH'` key, one byte, in the table that already drives the reader and the
writer both (§51.5) — five bytes of `drv_cfg_keys` and three of

doc_fixes.new_text:
A `'TH'` key, ver 3 and five bytes (the theme, §11.99's zoom and §79.4's
three), in the table that already drives the reader and the writer both
(§51.5) — five bytes of `drv_cfg_keys` and three of `drv_cfg_map`. The map
stores `[thm_kind]` like any plain setting; the unpack then calls `thm_set`,
which resolves the pens and owns both refusals — an unknown kind and Color
without colour (§76.12.1).
doc_fixes.why: driver.inc:971-972 `dw 'TH' / db 3, 5, CFG_THM`; the map stores thm_kind (driver.inc:910-911) and the unpack calls thm_set (driver.inc:4974-4984).
